revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For {Company}: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For {Company}: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For {Company}: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For {Company}: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For {Company}: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For {Company}: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For {Company}: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For {Company}: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For {Company}: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

arr.title: Annual recurring revenue
arr.content:
ARR is the annualised value of active subscriptions at period end -- the run-rate, not the period's revenue.

For {Company}: ARR growth leads reported revenue growth by roughly a year; a slowdown here shows up in revenue later.

What to watch:

  • Net new ARR per period
  • ARR growth versus revenue growth

subscription.title: Subscription mix
subscription.content:
Subscription revenue is recurring; services revenue (implementation, training) is lower-margin and lumpy.

For {Company}: a rising subscription share improves gross margin and predictability.

What to watch:

  • Subscription as a share of total revenue

customers.title: Customers
customers.content:
The number of paying customers at period end.

For {Company}: revenue growth decomposes into customer growth and revenue per customer; disclosure often stops when the count stalls.

What to watch:

  • Growth in customers versus growth in revenue
  • Whether the company still discloses the figure

nrr.title: Net revenue retention
nrr.content:
NRR is revenue from a cohort of customers a year later, including expansion and churn, as a percentage of the starting revenue.

For {Company}: above 100% means the existing base grows on its own; best-in-class SaaS runs 110-130%.

What to watch:

  • NRR trend
  • Gross retention if disclosed

churn.title: Churn
churn.content:
Churn is the share of customers or revenue lost in the period.

For {Company}: churn compounds: 2% monthly is 22% a year.

What to watch:

  • Direction of churn
  • Logo versus revenue churn

tpv.title: Total payment volume
tpv.content:
TPV is the gross value of payments processed -- the base the take rate is earned on.

For {Company}: revenue is TPV multiplied by take rate; volume growth and take-rate pressure often move in opposite directions.

What to watch:

  • TPV growth versus revenue growth
  • Mix shift toward lower-take-rate channels

processedVolume.title: Processed volume
processedVolume.content:
Gross value of transactions processed through the platform.

For {Company}: scale drives unit costs; watch the revenue earned per unit of volume.

What to watch:

  • Volume growth
  • Revenue per unit of volume

takeRate.title: Take rate
takeRate.content:
Take rate is net revenue as a percentage of volume processed or sold.

For {Company}: a falling take rate can be healthy (mix toward large customers) or not (pricing pressure); the filings say which.

What to watch:

  • Take-rate trend against volume growth

activeCustomers.title: Active customers
activeCustomers.content:
Customers who transacted in the trailing period.

For {Company}: revenue per active customer is the other half of the growth equation.

What to watch:

  • Active-customer growth
  • Revenue per active customer

gmv.title: Gross merchandise value
gmv.content:
GMV is the total value of goods sold through the platform, including third-party sellers.

For {Company}: revenue is a fraction of GMV (the take rate); GMV is the scale metric, revenue the monetisation metric.

What to watch:

  • GMV growth
  • Take rate on GMV

orders.title: Orders
orders.content:
The number of orders placed in the period.

For {Company}: orders times average order value equals sales; the split shows whether growth is volume or price.

What to watch:

  • Order growth
  • Orders per active customer

aov.title: Average order value
aov.content:
AOV is sales divided by orders.

For {Company}: AOV rising with flat orders means mix or pricing is doing the work.

What to watch:

  • AOV trend against inflation

cac.title: Customer acquisition cost
cac.content:
CAC as disclosed by the company -- marketing spend per new customer.

For {Company}: a proxy computed from marketing spend and net customer adds was wrong by 1.6-4.0x on another ticker; only the disclosed figure is charted.

What to watch:

  • CAC against revenue per customer (payback)

marketing.title: Marketing spend
marketing.content:
Marketing expense and its share of revenue.

For {Company}: marketing intensity is the growth lever; a business that cannot cut it without losing growth has weak organic demand.

What to watch:

  • Marketing as a percentage of revenue
  • Growth per marketing dollar

repeat.title: Repeat orders
repeat.content:
Orders from returning customers as a share of all orders.

For {Company}: a high repeat share lowers the acquisition cost per order.

What to watch:

  • Repeat share trend

mau.title: Active users
mau.content:
MAU and DAU are monthly and daily active users.

For {Company}: DAU / MAU is engagement; monetisation is revenue per user.

What to watch:

  • User growth
  • DAU/MAU ratio

affo.title: AFFO
affo.content:
AFFO (adjusted funds from operations) is a property owner's distributable cash: net income excluding revaluations, adjusted for maintenance capex and lease incentives.

For {Company}: the valuation capitalises AFFO at the cost of equity; statutory net income is dominated by revaluation noise.

What to watch:

  • AFFO per share growth
  • Payout ratio (DPS / AFFO per share)

nta.title: NTA per share
nta.content:
NTA per share is net tangible assets divided by shares -- the book value of the portfolio.

For {Company}: the share price relative to NTA is the market's view of the portfolio's valuation and management.

What to watch:

  • Discount or premium to NTA
  • NTA growth from revaluations versus retained cash

occupancy.title: Occupancy
occupancy.content:
The share of lettable space (or units) that is leased.

For {Company}: occupancy below the sector norm is the first sign of rental pressure.

What to watch:

  • Occupancy trend
  • Lease expiries in the next two years

walt.title: Weighted average lease term
walt.content:
WALT is the average remaining lease term, weighted by rent.

For {Company}: a longer WALT means more contracted income and less re-leasing risk.

What to watch:

  • WALT trend
  • Concentration of expiries

rental.title: Gross rental income
rental.content:
Rent received from tenants before property expenses.

For {Company}: compare with AFFO to see how much of rent reaches owners.

What to watch:

  • Like-for-like rental growth

nim.title: Net interest margin
nim.content:
NIM is net interest income as a percentage of interest-earning assets.

For {Company}: the core profitability metric of a lender; a few basis points move earnings materially.

What to watch:

  • NIM trend with the rate cycle
  • Funding cost versus lending yield

totalIncome.title: Total income
totalIncome.content:
Net interest income plus fees and other operating income.

For {Company}: the top line for a financial; revenue in the ordinary sense does not apply.

What to watch:

  • Income growth versus cost growth

aum.title: Assets under management
aum.content:
AUM is the value of client assets the firm manages or administers.

For {Company}: fee income scales with AUM; flows and market moves both drive it.

What to watch:

  • Net flows versus market performance

deposits.title: Deposits
deposits.content:
Customer deposits and cash held.

For {Company}: deposits are funding, not debt: the DCF does not subtract them as net debt.

What to watch:

  • Deposit growth and cost

nav.title: NAV per share
nav.content:
NAV per share is the net asset value of the portfolio per share.

For {Company}: the valuation compounds NAV and applies an exit discount; the share price discount to NAV is the second lever.

What to watch:

  • NAV total return
  • Discount to NAV versus history

netAssets.title: Net assets
netAssets.content:
Total portfolio value less liabilities.

For {Company}: growth here is NAV growth plus new capital raised.

What to watch:

  • Net assets against shares on issue

distributions.title: Distributions
distributions.content:
Cash distributed per share or unit.

For {Company}: a policy of paying a fixed percentage of NAV keeps NAV flat by design.

What to watch:

  • Distribution policy versus earnings

oraSales.title: ORA sales
oraSales.content:
Sales of occupation right agreements: new sales from developments and resales of existing units.

For {Company}: resale volumes drive deferred management fee realisation; new sales fund development.

What to watch:

  • Resale volumes against stock available
  • Pricing versus the housing market

dmf.title: Deferred management fees
dmf.content:
DMF accrues over a resident's tenure and is realised on resale.

For {Company}: the recurring, high-margin core of the model; reported net income is dominated by revaluations instead.

What to watch:

  • DMF growth against units in portfolio

units.title: Units in portfolio
units.content:
Retirement units and care beds operated.

For {Company}: the installed base that DMF and care fees are earned on.

What to watch:

  • Growth from development versus acquisition

development.title: Development
development.content:
Units delivered and the development margin earned on them.

For {Company}: development margin is cash realised on first sale; a fall signals build-cost or pricing pressure.

What to watch:

  • Units delivered against the pipeline
  • Development margin trend

underlying.title: Underlying profit
underlying.content:
Underlying profit removes unrealised revaluation gains from reported net income.

For {Company}: the valuation capitalises underlying profit; reported NPAT is not comparable year to year.

What to watch:

  • Underlying profit growth
  • Share of profit from resales versus new sales

aisc.title: All-in sustaining cost
aisc.content:
AISC is the total cost to produce an ounce, including sustaining capital, as defined by the World Gold Council.

For {Company}: the study-stage figure; the gap between AISC and the gold price is the project's margin per ounce.

What to watch:

  • AISC against the assumed gold price
  • Study revisions as the project advances

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For {Company}: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)
